gloss: to be the first to speak; to start things off

definitions.gloss: to be the first to speak; to start things off; to break the ice
definitions.explanation: To be the one who initiates a discussion, debate, or action. Often used when someone is the first to speak up or take action in a group setting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{議論|ぎろん}→議論：02650_giron⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{口火|くちび}を{切|き}った。
⟦{誰|だれ}も→誰も：18610_daremo⟧⟦{発言|はつげん}→発言：05099_hatsugen⟧⟦しない→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{口火|くちび}を{切|き}ることにした。
examples.english: Since nobody was speaking up, I decided to start things off.

examples.japanese: ⟦{反対|はんたい}{派|は}→反対派：30532_hantaiha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{口火|くちび}を{切|き}り、{次|つぎ}々⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{出|で}された。
examples.english: The representative of the opposition started things off, and opinions poured out one after another.

notes:
Originally a military term: ⟦{口火|くちび}→口火：27223_kuchibi⟧ refers to the fuse or primer of a firearm, so {口火|くちび}を{切|き}る literally meant 'to light the fuse' or 'to open fire.' Now used figuratively to mean being the first to speak or act, triggering a chain of events.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{口火|くちび}→口火：27223_kuchibi⟧ is the opening of a furnace or the touch hole of a cannon — the small ignition point that sets off the main charge. The metaphor extends to being the catalyst that sets a discussion or movement in motion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{議論|ぎろん}→議論：02650_giron⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{口火|くちび}を{切|き}る — to kick off a debate
- ⟦{批判|ひはん}→批判：03580_hihan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{口火|くちび}を{切|き}る — to be the first to criticize
- ⟦{改革|かいかく}→改革：04815_kaikaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{口火|くちび}を{切|き}る — to spark reform

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先陣|せんじん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ — to take the lead, to be at the vanguard; broader in scope, not limited to speech
- {火蓋|ひぶた}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ — to open hostilities; similar military origin, often used for the start of a battle or fierce competition
